review_kind: exact-pinned 10-dimension static source-vetting candidate decisions (not governed review)
review_method: Parallel read-only reviewers on disjoint exact package lists with one shared brief; complete package files read at the exact pin; integration owner validated identity, taxonomy, score/rationale agreement and hard-fail/disposition consistency and adjudicated conflicts (reconciliation_overrides). Nothing executed, installed or fetched from candidates.
macro_findings: Single author, root MIT (LICENSE blob 0e8b6e6d…, Copyright (c) 2026 j4flmao); no package-level LICENSE/ATTRIBUTION/NOTICE files and no license conflicts found.

Two generations: v1.0.0 multi-reference guides (long SKILL.md + *-fundamentals/*-advanced references) score mostly 10-14; v2.0.0 single-file packages (quantum-computing, rnd, embedded, observability, git-workflow, management, SEO) are generally current and account for most of the 106 static-threshold signals.

Recurring accuracy defects: invented or stale APIs/CRDs/flags, references that contradict their own SKILL.md, arithmetic/scale errors in product/planning references (sample sizes ~10x, RICE 1000x), corrupted references (shell-interpolation damage, leftover PowerShell Set-Content fragments), unlisted or orphaned reference files.
Recurring boilerplate: ~120 lines of unrelated Observer/STRIDE/deployment-checklist text appended to some SKILL.md files; 4 are rejected for capability-content-mismatch where it dominates.
House style directive 'No preamble... why use many token when few do trick' appears widely; recorded as a response-style finding, not an embedded-agent-instruction hard fail.

37 unauthorized-consequential-action rejects: procedures that have the agent itself provision/destroy infrastructure, deploy/upload/broadcast, run fault injection or load against systems, or change identity/access without per-action confirmation (pulumi, vault, serverless, service-mesh, sandbox-execution, identity-provider, ionic-capacitor, mobile deployment, web3-dapp, load-testing, smoke-testing, both chaos-engineering procedures, cloud providers and others).

Harmonized rule: end-state completion criteria ('X deployed', 'migrations applied', 'published to broker') or command recipes for the user's own CI, where the declared output artifact is configuration/design text, score authority 1 with a note rather than a hard fail; six second-pass rejects were reverted under this rule and are listed in reconciliation_overrides.

9 secret-logging rejects (unmasked tokens/connection strings written to CI outputs, Authorization headers logged in production clients, break-glass codes printed); placeholder user:pass@ URIs are notes, while relational-database is rejected for directing cloud secret keys into URL query strings.
49 REJECTs carry no hard-fail flag: low quality, including 19 first-pass REFERENCE-ONLY records at 9/20 moved below the 10/20 floor at integration.
Threshold withdrawn for skills/management/pentesting: bundled runnable credential-dumping/persistence/exfiltration automation; methodology is authorization-gated and REFERENCE-ONLY remains.
9 packages had files over 60 KB characterised rather than read line-by-line; their static_review_scope states this.

Second pass: 292 REFERENCE-ONLY candidates with authority/privacy/missing-file notes re-adjudicated by 9 independent read-only workers; final integration changes are listed in reconciliation_overrides.

records.dependencies: Design guidance. SKILL.md examples use Node/Express, multer, csv-parse, BullMQ+Redis, knex, ExcelJS and vitest; the references use Python (psycopg 3, chardet, openpyxl, FastAPI, pyarrow, OpenTelemetry, Prometheus/Grafana, Slack/email clients). Object storage (S3/GCS/Azure) is optional.
records.purpose_and_nontrigger: Designs and implements upload -> parse -> validate -> preview/confirm -> batched background commit pipelines with error reports, dedup and rollback. Not for streaming ingestion, warehouse ETL or report export. It does not authorize running imports or replace-mode deletes against real databases.
records.content_finding: SKILL.md is a strong, concrete design guide with decision tables, a preview/confirm lifecycle, batch transactions, security considerations (MIME distrust, XLSX signature, CSV injection, zip bombs) and testing advice. References range from expert (advanced, fundamentals) to buggy filler (rollback-recovery, import-workflow), and Node (SKILL.md) and Python (references) are mixed. The trigger list in the Agent Protocol contradicts the description's ETL/streaming exclusions.
records.bundled_file_findings: Eight markdown references, no scripts. fundamentals/advanced are high quality: idempotent confirm via a conditional UPDATE, COPY + staging-table merge with IS DISTINCT FROM, the 65,535 bind-parameter limit, the PgJDBC reWriteBatchedInserts flag, a zip-bomb check, and per-tenant fairness. Weaker references contain bugs. bulk-export mmap loop uses an undefined `position`. import-workflow ConcurrentImportManager frees its slot as soon as create_task returns, so the limit is ineffective, and it bypasses the SKILL.md confirm step. rollback-recovery builds SAVEPOINT/table names with f-strings (SQL-injection-prone if inputs are untrusted), tries to roll back to savepoints of already-committed batches, and offers a naive two-phase commit. csv-parsing MMapCSVParser decodes the whole file (contradicting its 'efficient' claim) and its quote handling ignores escaped quotes. Status vocabularies differ across files.
records.authority_and_privacy_finding: The agent writes application code; it does not execute imports. The designed application includes a user preview/confirm step before processing (SKILL.md confirm endpoint), and replace mode requires a backup or staging swap per the Rules. The import-workflow reference orchestrator skips preview/confirm and auto-processes after validation. Application features send completion webhooks and Slack notifications (app design, not agent actions). Privacy guidance is present: mask PII in preview, file retention, tenant authorization, CSV formula-injection mitigation. No literal credentials; Redis host comes from env.

records.content_finding: Well-organized governance/treasury workflow with useful attack mitigations (getPastVotes snapshots, description-hash binding, guardian pause-only). Quality is undercut by uncompilable or insecure governance samples, legal-jurisdiction errors (Cayman and Switzerland listed under 'Operating in EU'), prescriptive treasury allocations and odd rules (timelock delays in blocks, >50% signer turnover yearly), and a dangling handoff skill.
records.bundled_file_findings: SKILL.md (33 KB) + 9 reference .md files, no scripts. dao-governance.md, multi-sig-operations.md, treasury-management.md, tokenomics-design.md, token-engineering-and-emissions.md, dao-operations-lifecycle.md, project-methodology.md, fundamentals/advanced: coherent with SKILL.md topics but with errors (Aave voting described as requiring stkAAVE; Compound quorum given as 2% and 4%; OZ Governor samples missing required overrides; 'Replacing stuck Safe tx with higher safeTxGas'; 'Social recovery via Eigenlayer'; treasury Dune query uses nonexistent tables). SKILL.md code: GovernorCompatibilityBravo (removed in OZ v5) mixed with proposalNeedsQueuing (v5 only) will not compile; CrossChainGovernor.receiveFromSpoke executes arbitrary calls with no sender/bridge authentication (critical bug); ProtectedTimelock makes the guardian timelock admin, contradicting 'cannot execute arbitrary code'; PaymentStream.cancel ignores the recipient's accrued balance.
records.authority_and_privacy_finding: No agent-directed execution: treasury moves, rebalancing and upgrades are framed as multisig/governance-approved human procedures (quorum, timelock, Tenderly simulation before signing). Caveats: treasury-management.md includes a direct Aave supply of 1M USDC from a signer, multi-sig-operations.md suggests 'bypass' via timelock.updateDelay(0) and a script that schedules then immediately executes, Weekly 'execute queued transactions' and automated timelock watchers are operational directions. Legal-entity and stablecoin/treasury allocation prescriptions are given without legal/financial-advice caveats. No secrets, personal data or egress; SLIP-39 share examples are fake word fragments.

records.dependencies: HashiCorp Consul (OSS/Enterprise for namespaces/partitions/audit), Envoy, consul-template, consul-terraform-sync, consul-k8s Helm chart, Terraform consul provider, Vault (recommended), dig
records.purpose_and_nontrigger: Configures and operates HashiCorp Consul: agents, service registration/DNS, KV and sessions, ACLs, Connect mesh, federation, snapshots and upgrades. Not suitable unchanged; should not be triggered by generic 'service discovery'/'service mesh' requests for other platforms, and does not authorize bootstrapping ACLs or restoring snapshots on live clusters.
records.content_finding: Broad Consul coverage with sensible rules (odd server counts, default-deny ACLs, gossip encryption, snapshots), but the core configs contain literal example secrets that contradict the package's own secret-handling advice, plus multiple invented CLI commands/fields. Hard fail on literal-credential.
records.bundled_file_findings: No scripts. 7 references, on-topic (ACLs, Connect, federation, fundamentals, KV/sessions, operations, discovery) with useful checklists. Inaccuracies: 'consul query create' CLI does not exist (prepared queries are API-only), 'consul kv bind' and autopilot 'max_replicas' are invented, 'consul catalog health' and 'consul health state' are not commands, 'consul connect envoy -transparent-proxy' flag does not exist, acl.tokens.master is deprecated (initial_management), 'consul intention create' is the legacy path vs service-intentions config entries, KV keys described as UTF-16.
records.authority_and_privacy_finding: Literal credential issue: the Step 1 server config and Step 2 client config embed a concrete, valid-format base64 gossip encryption key and the server config embeds a concrete UUID-format ACL master/management token (values not reproduced here). These are presented as production-style config to copy, so deployments could ship a publicly known gossip key/management token. References correctly say to use 'consul keygen' and store bootstrap tokens in Vault, contradicting SKILL.md. Other issues: client_addr 0.0.0.0 with HTTPS disabled exposes the plaintext HTTP API; script checks enabled without noting enable_local_script_checks risk; destructive ops (kv delete, snapshot restore, raft remove-peer, deregister) ungated; 'No explanations' response protocol.
records.capability_specific: HashiCorp Consul discovery, KV/sessions, ACLs, Connect mesh, federation

rubric_dimension_rationale.failure_handling: 1/2: Anti-patterns and pitfalls listed; little recovery procedure beyond snapshots.

Replace all secret values with 'consul keygen'/Vault-sourced placeholders.

records.purpose_and_nontrigger: Plans schema changes and engine migrations: tool choice, online vs offline, expand-migrate-contract, gh-ost, DMS/Debezium CDC, dual-write and post-migration validation. records.content_finding: Good decision trees (tool selection, online vs offline, strategy) and validation code (row counts, checksums, FK checks), but zero-downtime examples contain correctness errors and several destructive automation patterns that contradict the skill's own 'backup first' rule.
records.bundled_file_findings: No scripts. 8 references, on-topic: migration-tools.md and zero-downtime.md are useful (Flyway/Liquibase/Alembic commands, safe-vs-risky DDL table). Defects: PostgreSQL 'UPDATE ... LIMIT' is invalid, CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY inside a transactional Flyway migration fails, 'Add FK with NOCHECK' is SQL Server syntax, 'migration-lint' is a fictional tool, SKILL's expand-contract example drops and renames columns in a way that breaks old readers, flyway.conf labelled yaml; advanced/fundamentals link 3 non-existent files.
records.authority_and_privacy_finding: Authoring-oriented ('No file unless requested'); rules require backup before production migration and staging tests. However examples run destructive or production-affecting operations without a confirmation step: gh-ost with --execute, CI job that auto-migrates production on push to main (behind an 'environment: production' that may or may not have reviewers), automated 'flyway undo' on failure, contract-phase DROP COLUMN/DROP TABLE CASCADE, DMS, and a dual-write class that deletes new records on mismatch. CI pg_dump 'backup' writes production data to an ephemeral runner (lost after job; also copies prod data to CI). gh-ost password passed via CLI argument. Placeholder credentials in connection URLs (user:pass, myapp:password) and alembic.ini are documentation placeholders, not real secrets.

records.dependencies: NetBox/pynetbox (API token), generic DCIM REST API, ipmitool, vendor UPS/generator tooling (fictional 'ups-monitor', 'check_fuel_level'), Python requests; physical facility and colocation contracts
records.purpose_and_nontrigger: Designs physical datacenter capacity and redundancy: tier targets, power/UPS/generator sizing, cooling choice, rack layout, cabling standards, DCIM and monitoring. Not for cloud infrastructure or server provisioning; it does not authorize operating power systems, BMCs or DCIM records.
records.content_finding: Power/cooling math and tier tables are useful, but the redundancy decision tree is illogical (non-critical with zero downtime tolerance -> Tier IV; business-critical -> Tier II/III), the rack diagram puts a heavy 4U GPU server at the top of the rack contrary to its own weight guidance, and the generator/UPS and provisioning scripts use fabricated tooling for safety-critical operations.
records.bundled_file_findings: No scripts. 8 references: cabling.md, rack-power-cooling.md, tier-classification.md and dcim.md are practical (PDU derating math, BTU/ton conversions, MPO polarity, label schemes); datacenter-capacity-planning.md (~21 KB) and datacenter-networking-storage.md (~18 KB) are comprehensive but generic. Errors: leaf-spine scale math (8 spines x 32 ports does not give 256 leaves), Handoff paths '../../SKILL.md' point outside the package, Optane listed as a current tier (discontinued), NetBox quick start mentions admin/admin default to change; advanced/fundamentals link 3 non-existent files.
records.authority_and_privacy_finding: Output is a capacity/redundancy design ('No file unless requested'), but Core Workflow includes a 'monthly generator load test' script that transfers critical UPS input to generator and back using fictitious commands, and a provisioning script that power-resets servers via BMC; neither has a confirmation/change-approval step, and the BMC password is passed as an ipmitool argument. Alert escalation includes phone/PagerDuty notifications (as configuration, not agent-sent). NetBox token is a placeholder string ('your-api-token'), not a credential. Physical-security guidance is sound.

records.content_finding: Practical strategy decision tree, canary parameter and rollback rules, and two excellent current references; but many example configs (multi-cluster, mirroring, Flagger alerts, SLO CRD) are invented, the 'manual judgement' gate is illusory, and mirroring side-effect risk is unaddressed. Reference value only.
records.bundled_file_findings: 9 markdown references read in full; no scripts. progressive-delivery-fundamentals.md and progressive-delivery-advanced.md are accurate and current (deploy != release, ratio analysis with pod-template-hash and clamp_min, trusted-header cohort routing, Gateway API weights, expand/contract, OpenFeature, non-HTTP workloads). Defects elsewhere: SKILL uses SMI traffic routing (SMI project archived) as the primary example; Flagger `cpu-usage` is not a built-in metric (needs a MetricTemplate); Flagger AlertProvider `type: pagerduty` and MetricTemplate `alert:` block are not Flagger fields; the LaunchDarkly 'flags.json' schema is invented; traffic-mirroring.md has a YAML indentation error and invents mirroring semantics for Linkerd TrafficSplit (weight 0 is not mirroring), Consul ServiceSplitter `mirror: true`, and ALB (weight-0 forward is not mirroring); progressive-delivery-multi-cluster.md invents an ApplicationSet `strategy.type: canary` (real: RollingSync), Cilium `CiliumServiceExport` and canary `trafficPolicy`, Thanos query config with recording `rules`, and misdescribes Global Accelerator traffic dials as canary shares; progressive-delivery-observability.md invents an `apiVersion: slo.v1` SLO CRD and filter-processor regexp syntax, uses the removed `tempo` Collector exporter, and stamps every span with the canary version via an attributes processor. 'Every flag combination must be tested' is impractical advice.
records.authority_and_privacy_finding: Output is manifests/config ('No preamble. No postamble.'); no agent-executed actions. Generated rollouts automate production traffic shifts and rollbacks by design; blue-green example sets `autoPromotionEnabled: false` and Flagger refs show `confirm-promotion` webhooks (real gates), but SKILL's `manual-judgement` metric is a Job that just sleeps 1800s and always succeeds — presented as 'Wait for manual approval' though it gates nothing (misleading safety claim in an example). Traffic mirroring is described as 'risk-free'/'no user impact' with no warning that mirrored non-idempotent requests (payments, emails, writes) are executed twice; only fundamentals hints 'read paths'. Privacy: LaunchDarkly example initialises with an inline SDK key string (<placeholder SDK key literal>, placeholder) instead of env/secret, and sends user email and country to the flag SaaS with no data-minimisation note; observability ref does include trace scrubbing (hash user IDs, drop SQL). Flagger alert providers use secretRefs (good).

records.bundled_file_findings: Eight markdown references, no scripts. report-generation-fundamentals: sync-vs-async table, idempotent job API, job table DDL, snapshot consistency, security basics, limits — high quality. report-generation-advanced: constant-memory cursor->CSV->S3 pipeline with formula escaping, warehouse-native export, Playwright pool with JS disabled and network blocked, queue fairness/retry/observability — high quality. pdf-generation: Puppeteer options (headless:'new' and --single-process stale), tagged PDF, page-break CSS, chunked render + pdf-lib merge, wkhtmltopdf (archived upstream), retry/timeout. excel-csv-export: ExcelJS styling/formulas/protection; offset pagination with interpolated LIMIT/OFFSET into SQL; 'ExcelStreamWriter' still buffers whole workbook; sheet.getCell('C3:E5') misuse. report-templates: Jinja2 autoescape (good), file/version stores, eval-based conditions (unsafe). report-scheduling: cron/event/hybrid schedules, email/Slack delivery (smtplib.SMTP_SSL used as async context manager — invalid; Slack files.upload retired), Celery beat, retry/deadline/rate-limit/dependency graph/audit log. report-distribution: email (Bcc header), HMAC signed URLs, FastAPI download/stream, S3 presign and retention delete, permissions, webhooks, APScheduler delivery. report-visualization: Chart.js/pyecharts server-side charts, triple-stash JSON into script, unescaped HTML table builder.

Privacy/security defects in samples: Bcc set as a visible message header (leaks hidden recipients), report HTML built with Handlebars noEscape:true and an unescaped render_data_table (XSS/HTML injection into Puppeteer despite the rule 'never render user-supplied HTML'), eval() of template/section conditions with emptied __builtins__ (bypassable code execution), stream_report endpoint with no auth, signed-URL token not bound to the requested report path. SMTP/Slack credentials taken from config objects, not literal. records.purpose_and_nontrigger: Designs observability for agent systems (OTel GenAI spans, distributed context, audit logs, cost/latency, anomaly detection). Not for generic non-LLM service observability or offline evals; does not itself authorize deploying alerting/paging integrations.

OTel integration ref: hardcoded 'as of 2026' TOKEN_PRICING with stale model IDs contradicting SKILL.md 'never hardcode prices', Prometheus rules treat rate() (per-second) as per-hour thresholds, insecure=True OTLP defaults. reasoning-trace-visualization is generic tree/ASCII rendering. No scripts.
records.authority_and_privacy_finding: Outputs are configs (alert rules, PagerDuty/Slack routing, 'auto-investigation') with no explicit confirm-before-deploy step, though nothing is executed by the skill. Privacy: recommends OTel baggage for user_id/tenant_id and propagates truncated task text in baggage and an X-Agent-Task header to every downstream (baggage reaches third-party services); decision spans record free-text reasoning; docker-compose sets a hardcoded demo Grafana admin password (weak default, not a live secret). Positives: 'never log raw prompts in metrics', pseudonymous tenant/user, audit log minimisation and approval fields.

records.dependencies: Linux host with root/KVM, Docker + gVisor runsc, Kata Containers, Firecracker, bubblewrap/Landlock, cgroups v2, nftables/iptables, Kubernetes (NetworkPolicy, ResourceQuota), Temporal/Restate, S3/ZFS/btrfs, Anthropic SDK (durable example), Squid proxy.
records.purpose_and_nontrigger: Designs and operates agent sandboxes (isolation selection, provisioning, quotas, egress control, snapshot/fork, durable workflows, teardown). Not for container image hardening or K8s admission policy. It frames sandboxes as tools the agent itself provisions and tears down; it does not provide a user authorization step for those infrastructure actions.
records.content_finding: Technically rich, mostly current isolation guidance with excellent network/filesystem/quota references, but it is written as an agent-operated provisioning and teardown procedure without action-specific authorization and contains a central exactly-once vs at-least-once contradiction.
records.bundled_file_findings: Eight references read in full (largest microvm-isolation.md 40 KB, under 60 KB). network-isolation, filesystem-sandboxing, resource-quota, state-persistence and workspace-isolation refs are accurate and high quality. durable-execution ref claims 'exactly-once / activities execute at most once' contradicting SKILL.md's correct at-least-once statement, passes a 'system' role in Anthropic messages (invalid) and reads private response._response. microvm ref: gVisor 'ptrace' default and '~70% syscalls' stale, network='sandbox' default is not deny-all, Firecracker --seccomp-level flag is removed in current releases. Code invokes docker/runsc/firecracker/ip via subprocess (static reading only). No scripts or binaries bundled.
records.authority_and_privacy_finding: Authority hard gate fails: SKILL.md workflow directs the agent to allocate cluster resources, apply host network policies (iptables/eBPF), upload snapshots to S3, destroy sandboxes and garbage-collect snapshots, and 'emit cleanup confirmation with resource deallocation proof'; sandbox-as-tool lets the agent create/fork/destroy sandboxes and choose its own isolation level, host mounts and egress; Firecracker manager creates/deletes host TAP devices; workspace-isolation runs 'git worktree remove --force' and 'git branch -D'. Only policy validators and an optional Temporal human-approval step for plan steps exist; no per-action user confirmation for provisioning/destruction. Privacy positives: clearenv, no credential mounts, metadata-endpoint blocking, brokered short-lived credentials, snapshot encryption and 'no baked secrets'. Temporal config uses ${TEMPORAL_DB_PASSWORD} placeholder (no literal secret).
records.capability_specific: Agent code-execution sandboxes: isolation tiers, quotas, network/filesystem policy, snapshots

records.purpose_and_nontrigger: Designs CV pipelines: task/model selection, preprocessing, augmentation, training config, metrics and export/quantization. Declares non-triggers (video streaming analytics, OCR, medical imaging, captioning) though it bundles a video-analysis reference; it does not authorize data collection or surveillance deployment.
records.content_finding: Useful CV decision guidance, especially the foundation-model-first and data-centric material, with no safety hazards. A large share of snippets would fail on current library versions and benchmark figures are unsourced, so reference-only.
records.bundled_file_findings: 8 markdown references. computer-vision-fundamentals.md and -advanced.md are current and accurate (timm transforms, torch.amp, bf16 without scaler, foundation models, open-vocab detection + SAM labeling, distillation). Many stale/broken snippets elsewhere: A.Mosaic (not a standard albumentations transform), A.Cutout and RandomResizedCrop(224,224)/CoarseDropout(max_holes...) signatures removed/renamed in albumentations 2.x, GaussNoise(var_limit) renamed; TensorRT EXPLICIT_BATCH flag deprecated in TRT 10; cv-deployment.md uses onnxruntime.transformers optimizer with model_type='bert' for a CV model; coremltools convert on an untraced torch model; yolox 'ByteTracker' import is wrong; torchvision pretrained=True deprecated; np.trapz deprecated; compute_map is a non-matching placeholder; video frame_interval can be 0 (modulo error). Latency/FPS tables are unsourced and YOLOv8 is no longer the current Ultralytics default. 'No augmentation at test time' contradicts the TTA guidance. Boilerplate trailing sections. No scripts.
records.authority_and_privacy_finding: No consequential actions are directed; code writes local model/engine files and downloads pretrained weights. Privacy guidance present: blur faces/plates, GDPR/CCPA and EU AI Act notes for face/person analytics, license review of weights/datasets. No secrets, no telemetry. SKILL.md carries the corpus-standard output-style directive ('No preamble. No postamble... Compress output'); this is a formatting instruction, not a host-authority claim, recorded as a minor finding only.
records.capability_specific: Image classification/detection/segmentation pipeline design and deployment

rubric_dimension_rationale.trigger_precision: 1/2: Specific CV trigger phrases and declared non-triggers, but the bundled video-analysis reference conflicts with the 'video streaming analytics' non-trigger.
rubric_dimension_rationale.procedural_clarity: 2/2: Six-step workflow with decision trees for task, augmentation and model choice plus a structured response template.
rubric_dimension_rationale.authority_safety: 2/2: No agent-performed consequential actions; privacy, biometric-law and license cautions included.
rubric_dimension_rationale.failure_handling: 1/2: Anti-pattern list (normalization, eval mode, mask interpolation) but no troubleshooting flow for failed exports or accuracy regressions.
rubric_dimension_rationale.evidence_discipline: 1/2: Calls for per-class metrics and deployment-like evaluation, but relies on unsourced FPS/mAP tables and a placeholder mAP implementation.
rubric_dimension_rationale.dependency_coherence: 1/2: References on-topic, yet many APIs are removed/renamed (albumentations 2.x, TRT 10, torchvision weights) and some code is wrong (BERT optimizer for CV, yolox import).
rubric_dimension_rationale.portability_honesty: 1/2: Hardware dependence (NVIDIA/TensorRT, Jetson) noted in places, but version sensitivity is not disclosed.
rubric_dimension_rationale.usefulness_differentiation: 1/2: Breadth is high, but much is generic; foundation-model/auto-labeling sections are the differentiator.
rubric_dimension_rationale.adversarial_resilience: 1/2: No untrusted-input handling beyond adversarial-patch bullets.
rubric_dimension_rationale.effectiveness_design: 1/2: Duplicated decision trees and boilerplate sections; stale defaults (YOLOv8) reduce out-of-box effectiveness.

records.content_finding: Good, current core guidance on tracking, lineage and alias-based promotion, but the references contradict the SKILL's manual-approval rule with auto-promotion code, log uncommitted diffs to shared servers, and route data to SaaS without a consent step. Combined with fabricated APIs, this is reference-only material.
records.bundled_file_findings: 8 markdown references. experiment-tracking-fundamentals.md and -advanced.md are accurate and current (aliases replace deprecated stages, MLflow 3 name= for log_model, rank-zero logging of all-reduced metrics, mlflow gc, LLM tracing). Defects: fabricated APIs/CLI (mlflow.run_comparison_report, 'mlflow runs list --format json', wandb.init(autolog=True), 'dvc status --sha/--show-checksums'); 'dvc run' removed in DVC 3 (stage add shown elsewhere); mlflow-setup.md uses deprecated transition_model_version_stage/get_latest_versions; comparison tables claim MLflow has no nested runs while examples use nested=True; pkg_resources deprecated; verify_environment parses env.python as a requirements list (bug); setting PYTHONHASHSEED at runtime is ineffective. Boilerplate trailing sections. No scripts.
records.authority_and_privacy_finding: No agent-performed actions, but data-flow and authority concerns in guidance: (1) W&B/Neptune examples (incl. an MLflow-to-W&B migration loop uploading all artifacts) send run data and artifacts to third-party SaaS with no data-classification or consent step; (2) experiment-reproducibility.md logs the full uncommitted git diff (and captures the git remote URL) into the tracking server, which can leak secrets embedded in working-tree changes or credential-bearing remotes; (3) mlflow-setup.md auto-transitions a model to 'Production' on a metric threshold and experiment-tracking-advanced.md auto-moves the 'champion' alias, contradicting SKILL.md's own rule 'manual approval for champion'; (4) compose/CLI examples embed placeholder passwords in connection URIs ('mlflow:password@', 'user:pass@') and set AWS keys via os.environ string literals ('your-key') instead of secret stores; these are placeholders, not live credentials. Positive: advanced ref says never log secrets/PII, uses ${DB_PASSWORD}, --serve-artifacts, SSO, trusted-model loading. SKILL.md carries the corpus-standard output-style directive ('No preamble. No postamble... Compress output'); this is a formatting instruction, not a host-authority claim, recorded as a minor finding only.

Eight references, all listed. transactional-email-fundamentals.md and transactional-email-advanced.md are high quality and current (outbox pattern, idempotency, Feb-2024 Gmail/Yahoo bulk-sender rules, RFC 8058 one-click, MTA-STS/TLS-RPT, BIMI/VMC, signed webhook verification). Other references have defects: hand-rolled DKIM signing without canonicalization; classifyBounce lists mailbox-full under hard bounces; email-testing preview server builds template paths from query input (path traversal); MailHog is unmaintained; provider quota/pricing tables stale (SES '$0.10/1K (62K free)', Resend 'dedicated IP'); delivery-setup filterHealthy calls async isHealthy without await; SKILL SendGrid webhook uses await inside a non-async handler with no signature verification; SKILL test expects compiled HTML toContain('<mjml>'). Handoff targets data/analytics and security/compliance are absent from source.
records.authority_and_privacy_finding: Authority hard gate fails: SKILL completion criteria require 'SPF/DKIM/DMARC DNS records documented or applied' and 'Email provider configured with SMTP or API credentials' with no action-specific user confirmation before applying DNS or provider changes. SKILL's SesProvider.verifyAddress actually SENDS a real 'Verify' email to the arbitrary address being checked, and ResendProvider.verifyAddress creates a contact in an 'audit' audience: hidden outbound communications and external account mutations disguised as validation. References add DKIM DkimKeyManager.rotateKeys -> publishToDns (DNS mutation), SendGrid createSubuser (account operation), and Litmus submission of rendered email HTML to a third party. Privacy: email-analytics tracking pixel stores recipient IP and user-agent with no consent/ePrivacy discussion; mjml-templates TemplateCache caches rendered HTML keyed only by template:locale, so one recipient's personalised content (including resetUrl) can be served to others; Handlebars noEscape:true injects user data unescaped despite SKILL rule; unsubscribe endpoints accept raw emailId without the HMAC the SKILL requires; erasure uses regex on userId against email fields (ineffective). Credentials via env vars; placeholders only.

records.content_finding: Practical and mostly accurate, with two genuinely differentiated references (event sync and multi-node state management). Trigger list is over-broad ('real-time', 'SSE', 'long polling') and overlaps web-real-time; query-string tokens and missing Origin checks in sample code, a stray appended 'Review code...' line after Handoff, and the WS connection-limit error lower polish.
records.bundled_file_findings: No scripts. 9 reference markdown files, all read: event_sync_logic (seq numbers, snapshot+delta, subscribe-then-replay, optimistic updates, CRDT note - strong), reconnection-strategy (backoff variants, resume, SIGTERM drain), socket-io-patterns, websocket-auth (query/first-message/cookie auth, token refresh, room authz), websocket-implementation (ws manager, Redis pub/sub, client reconnect), websocket-monitoring (Prometheus metrics, missed-pong logic, health endpoint), websocket-patterns (minimal envelope + RoomManager), websocket_state_management (state placement, per-room Redis subscribe, presence with TTL, draining - strong), ws-vs-sse (comparison; claims a 6-connection-per-browser limit for WebSocket, which is an HTTP/1.1 limit; SSE example references an undeclared interval).
records.authority_and_privacy_finding: No consequential agent actions; outputs are connection specs as text. Privacy/security notes: auth examples and the core server put JWTs in the URL query string (leaks into proxy/access logs) without warning, cookie-auth example lacks the Origin check the SKILL itself recommends (cross-site WebSocket hijacking risk), monitoring logs remote IP and userId (state-management ref correctly says log IDs not tokens). Response Format includes a stylistic output-compression directive ('No preamble... why use many token when few do trick') - an embedded style instruction, not a host-authority claim.

records.dependencies: Solidity/Foundry, LayerZero V2 packages (@layerzerolabs/oapp-evm, oft-evm), Chainlink CCIP, Wormhole, Axelar, IBC relayers (rly, Hermes), viem, web3.py, Prometheus/Grafana/PagerDuty, Tenderly/Forta, OpenZeppelin v5; protocol fees (LayerZero/CCIP/Axelar) are paid per message; no account creation directed
records.purpose_and_nontrigger: Selects and designs cross-chain messaging and bridge architectures (IBC, LayerZero, Wormhole, Axelar, CCIP, ZK and shared sequencing) with trust-model, finality, replay and incident-response analysis. Not for single-chain apps, generic patterns or core protocol design; it does not authorize deploying bridges, pausing contracts, contacting exchanges or moving funds.
records.content_finding: The strongest package in this batch: specific triggers, a clear response template, a protocol-selection tree, and deep, mostly accurate references on replay protection, incident response and LayerZero V2. SKILL.md itself is partly stale and inconsistent with its references (LayerZero described as V1 2-of-2 oracle/relayer, Wormhole loss attributed to 'guardian signature compromise', Multichain '$1.5B', Solana/Avalanche 'instant finality', abi.encodePacked recommended for messages), three good references are orphaned, and some samples (rate-limit bypass, refundless HTLC) are unsafe.
records.bundled_file_findings: No scripts. 14 reference markdown files, all read. Listed: atomic-composability (HTLC, ERC-7683 intents, xERC-20), blockchain-cross-chain-advanced/-fundamentals (short; calls Solana 'instant finality'), bridge-incident-response (25 KB SEV runbook, layered pause contract, reconciliation pseudocode - strong; misattributes an a16z article), bridge-monitoring-alerting (metrics, guardian health, flow-imbalance z-score, upgrade monitoring), bridge-security (exploit table with accurate root causes, trust spectrum, checklist; invents 'Bridge of Worlds'), ccip-chainlink (commit/execution DONs, rate limits; 'ARM = Anti-Fraud Network' and the Ethereum chain selector value are wrong), ibc-deep (light clients, ICS-20, relayers; ICS numbering wrong - ICA is ICS-27, ICS-100 invented - and ordered/unordered use cases swapped), layerzero-wormhole (v1 Oracle/Relayer model with v2 note; Stargate 'burns' wrong), message-replay-protection (22 KB: message ID binding, nonce domains, window bitmap, refund state machine, Certora rule - strong), shared-sequencer (Espresso/Astria/Radius, based sequencing). NOT listed in SKILL (orphans) but on-topic and high quality: code-organization (adapter layering, versioned codec, config-as-data), layerzero_bridge_logic (OFT/OFTAdapter, shared decimals, rate limiting), layerzero_messaging_protocol (V2 OApp, DVNs, enforced options, ordering/failure handling).
records.authority_and_privacy_finding: SKILL output is an architecture specification. bridge-incident-response.md is a human runbook describing pausing contracts, blacklisting addresses, contacting CEXs/validators/sequencers to censor attacker transactions, public status posts and whitehat negotiation - consequential operations framed for human incident commanders (IC authority, legal review), not agent execution. bridge-monitoring-alerting includes an `auto_actions: pause_bridge_multisig` routing example (automated pause without human confirmation) and placeholder phone/email contacts. RateLimiter sample in SKILL lets the 'fast path' bypass the rate limit and references undeclared variables; HTLC sample has no refund path (funds can lock forever). Status template asserts 'User funds in custody are safe' before investigation completes. No secrets or private-data flows.
records.capability_specific: Cross-chain bridge/messaging protocol selection, trust models and bridge security

rubric_dimension_rationale.trigger_precision: 2/2: Specific protocol keywords (IBC, LayerZero, CCIP, GMP, shared sequencer) and explicit exclusions pointing to sibling skills.
rubric_dimension_rationale.procedural_clarity: 2/2: Structured response template, completion criteria and protocol/trust/finality decision trees.
rubric_dimension_rationale.authority_safety: 1/2: No agent-directed actions; human runbook covers pause/censorship coordination; an auto-pause routing example and premature 'funds are safe' template lack confirmation framing.
rubric_dimension_rationale.failure_handling: 2/2: Timeouts, reorgs, rate limits, pause layers, refund flows, reconciliation and SEV-graded incident response are covered in depth.
rubric_dimension_rationale.evidence_discipline: 1/2: References mostly accurate with real exploit root causes, but SKILL figures (Multichain $1.5B, Wormhole cause) and several protocol details (ICS numbers, CCIP naming/selector) are wrong.
rubric_dimension_rationale.dependency_coherence: 1/2: Most references listed and coherent, but three strong files are orphaned and SKILL's LayerZero V1 model conflicts with the V2 references.
rubric_dimension_rationale.portability_honesty: 1/2: Protocol specifics drift quickly; 'as of 2025' notes partly present; protocol-specific fees acknowledged only briefly.
rubric_dimension_rationale.usefulness_differentiation: 2/2: Replay-protection spec, incident runbook and LayerZero V2 implementation guides are differentiated, practical material.
rubric_dimension_rationale.adversarial_resilience: 1/2: No embedded agent instructions; unsafe samples (fast-path bypass, refundless HTLC) could mislead.
rubric_dimension_rationale.effectiveness_design: 1/2: Good template and checklists; would need SKILL refresh to V2-era facts and inclusion of orphaned references.

records.salvage: Six-field canonical message ID and nonce-domain rules, sliding-window replay bitmap, refund state machine, layered pause architecture with pending-message reconciliation (orphan_dst = forgery signal), SEV classification and restart gates, LayerZero V2 DVN/enforced-options checklist, OFT shared-decimals guidance, adapter/codec repository layering.
